performer.name: The Jobber
performer.stance: veteran who loses for a living; proud craftsman of defeat, tender and dry, telling the trade's secrets on a borrowed entrance theme

structure: locker-room confession on a borrowed entrance theme: the roster, how the trick works, who decides, when it gets real, the finish, his one choice
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about the psychology of professional wrestling. A performer who loses matches for a living walks the audience through the roles, tricks and business of the show on the night of a match.
bestOfReason: Roster 1-4: face, heel, tweener and the performer's own card - who is who before anyone touches.
The trick 9, 11, 13, 14: selling, overselling, the audio lie, the stomp - he shows the craft and still asks to be believed.
Mind games 17, 22: the sacred mask and the snake bag - fear and identity before the bell.
Who decides 45, 46, 49: booker, spot caller, hard cam - the ending is written, the middle is sweat, the lens decides what happened.
The empty years 30, 31: the pop that never comes and the fake crowd - the one sad stretch.
When it gets real 35, 55: the unplanned injury and the police that keep the secret he is busy telling.
Finish 41, 42, 56: the finisher, the near-fall, the retirement that is never final.

three slaps of the mat, then the band hits

beats: Jobbers don't get entrance music. I borrowed somebody's tonight, so we'll be quick before he wants it back.
Twenty years I've been losing on Big Bad Brain Wrestling. Clean, every night, on purpose. Nobody alive does it better.
You, front row, with the sign. You paid to watch me lose. Good. Let me tell you who does it to me.

beats.text: The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.
The Heel: brutal, sneaky moves. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener: the audience decides to cheer for you on their own. You don't ask for it.
The Jobber: isolated and picked apart. You exist to make the other guy look good.
When defeated, you may choose who defeats you. That is your only control.

beats: Now I'll show you how the trick works. Then I'll still make you believe it.

beats.text: The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.
The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality. A mockery of the sport.
The Thigh Slap: slapping the thigh when kicking. A loud sound suggests impact. An audio lie.
The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.

beats: Some guys get in your head before you touch.

beats.text: The Sacred Mask: kayfabe sacred to their identity. The biggest identifier. Never remove it.
The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.

beats: You want to know who wins? Not us. Ask upstairs.

beats.text: The Booker: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.

beats.pre: In the ring we keep it quiet.
beats.text: The Spot Caller: calling moves in the ring. A basic outline, filled in with sweat.

beats.pre: And we turn to the lens.
beats.text: The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.

beats: I did a whole year of this next one.

beats.text: The Empty Arena: taped in empty arenas, pausing for a pop that never comes. Surreal.
The Green Screen Crowd: a failed attempt to hide the emptiness. Audio sweetening on a lie.

beats: Then one night, nobody books it.

beats.text: The Real Injury: Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post. The crowd goes nuts: it's real.

beats.pre: Which is why I never told you any of this.
beats.text: The Kayfabe Police: protecting the business. Keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Finisher: the Leg Drop. The most important moment. If this hits, go home.
The False Finish: the art of the near-fall, kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical.
The Retirement Match: leaning on the fourth wall. Rising, and falling. See you next season.

beats: My pick for tonight is you, front row, sign and all. You knew the ending, and you stood up at two point nine anyway.
Out there they all sell it and swear it's real. In here we tell you it's fake and give you everything. Choose your liars carefully.
